correctness.rationale: In A the vertex quotient is commutative and two arrows multiply to zero. For e:s→t each coefficient is (α_s−α_t)v_e−(β_s−β_t)u_e, and [e_s,e]=e. For r pairs, concatenating their diagonal coefficients gives q^(2r) possible labels; on a supported edge, an equal endpoint label would force zero. Conversely, for any proper support coloring with those labels, one differing diagonal coordinate supplies a nonzero coefficient in a local linear equation, so the arrow variables solve independently for the required targets. This includes the empty sum at zero and the width attained by taking all arrows nonzero. For a single pair unequal endpoints give q solutions per edge for every output, while equal endpoints give q² for zero and none otherwise. Expanding the extra factor on each nonsupported arrow contracts sets of forced equalities, retaining supported edges (including loops, which give zero colorings). This accounts for opposite/parallel arrows separately and uses field rank, not a prime-field assumption. Over F₂, K5 alone among its support subgraphs needs more than four colors: every proper subgraph allows a nonadjacent pair to share a color. Thus exactly the all-one target has length two. Orienting any graph by a total order preserves colorability; all arrows supported reduces 4-colorability to variable-input membership, and a proposed color assignment or bracket pair is a polynomial certificate. The reduction is not a fixed-algebra assertion. Ran python3 /workspace/reproductions/quivers.py: 140,969 ordered pairs in three cases over F₂,F₃,F₄, using path-basis multiplication and comparing all target populations with the contraction count, including mixed orientations/multiplicity. Example F₄ two opposite arrows: 7936 for zero and 3840 for each of the 15 nonzero targets. Independently checked all 1024 binary K5 supports and verified a two-bracket witness by multiplication. Uploaded verifier was inspected, not run; finite checks are not the universal proof.
